ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct mandatory screening against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, EU consolidated list, UK HMT consolidated list, and the Republic of Korea's domestic designation lists published by the Financial Services Commission and KoFIU. Screen every shareholder, director, beneficial owner, and authorized signatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs), their immediate family members and close associates, before incorporation and continuously thereafter. Positive hits require enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and, where required, freezing of assets and suspicious-transaction reporting to KoFIU; negative news and adverse-media research must be documented and retained for at least five years.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 2798, as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-70 (Limited Liability Company / Yuhan Hoesa); Commercial Act Article 288 (Contents of Articles of Incorporation) and Article 292 (Date of Incorporation); Commercial Registration Rules; Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of Yuhan Hoesa, operating through the Supreme Court of Korea i-registration online portal and the in-person registry counter.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa / LLC), submitted on the prescribed commercial registration form, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation and supporting contributor and officer documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean law does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. The Articles may provide for zero or nominal capital. Capital may be subscribed as cash or in-kind, and paid-in receipts must be obtained and retained. No blocked escrow account is mandated; however, funds must be actually paid or contributed before the District Court Registry will accept the incorporation registration. Registration tax and court filing fee are assessed in KRW based on the registered capital, with an approximate USD-equivalent state fee of 120 for a low-capital entity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE INITIAL DIRECTORS AND MEMBERS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT ON [DATE]. WHEREAS, Yuhan Hoesa has been formed as a limited liability company under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; and WHEREAS, the notarized Articles of Incorporation establish the members, capital, business purpose, registered office, and management structure; and WHEREAS, the company intends to be registered and to implement its statutory and commercial formalities; and WHEREAS, the initial members and directors are authorized to undertake all acts necessary to perfect the incorporation. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. Every subscription set forth in the Articles of Incorporation is ratified, accepted, and directed to be paid. The Representative Director is directed to collect capital contributions, issue contribution receipts, and confirm full payment of each subscriber's contribution prior to registration. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office stated in the Articles is adopted as the company's principal legal office. The Representative Director is authorized to execute or amend the office lease, obtain a lease certificate, and notify the District Court Registry and National Tax Service. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The company shall open corporate bank accounts with a licensed bank in the Republic of Korea. The Representative Director and any additional authorized signatory designated by the Representative Director are jointly empowered to execute account documents, deposit and disburse funds in the ordinary course, arrange online banking, and maintain control over funds until the members or a subsequent resolution determine otherwise. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. [NAME] is appointed Representative Director and legal representative of the company. [NAME] is appointed Director. [NAME] is appointed Auditor to the extent required by law or prudent corporate practice. Each appointed officer accepts the office and shall exercise all powers and duties prescribed by the Commercial Act, the Articles, and this resolution. 5. GENERAL DELEGATION. Each officer is authorized to appear before notaries public, the District Court Registry, banks, tax offices, and municipal offices; to sign all registration, tax, license, and account applications; to affix or procure the corporate seal; to pay fees; and to take every step necessary to carry out the incorporation and the lawful business of the company. 6. EFFECTIVENESS. This resolution takes effect immediately and continues in full force until revoked or amended by a subsequent written resolution of the members or directors. ADOPTED this [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve company name and notarize the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea i-registration online registry (www.iros.go.kr) and a Korean notary public for authentication.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a corporate name availability search using the i-registration portal and reserve the exact English or Korean name of Yuhan Hoesa. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean legal format, listing each member, capital contribution, address of the registered office, business purpose (no-code website builder / software activity), duration, and management composition. The articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public before filing. The notary will identify the subscribers, verify their legal capacity, and certify their signatures. Do not proceed to court registration until the notarized original is in hand.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of each member/subscriber
Draft Articles of Incorporation prepared in Korean
Power of attorney if filing through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity, select a new name and reserve it; if notarization is delayed due to missing identification, obtain an apostilled passport or corporate ID and arrange an earlier notary slot. Refiling after correction incurs no substantive penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Effect capital contribution and obtain contribution certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea where the incorporators open a temporary or declared-purpose capital collection account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization but before lodging the court application, complete the capital contribution process. If capital is declared, open a temporary or declared-purpose bank account in the intended corporate name, or cause each member to wire funds to a designated account. Obtain a bank certificate or deposit receipt showing the account holder and the amount deposited. For in-kind capital, obtain an asset transfer agreement and a valuation certificate if required. The Representative Director must confirm that the aggregate contributed amount or appraised in-kind value matches the Articles. Retain all contribution evidence for submission to the Registry.
required_dossiers: Bank contribution certificate or deposit receipt
Remittance confirmation records for each member
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening due to the absence of a registration number, request a temporary incorporator account; if the contribution certificate is challenged, obtain a corrected bank statement or a notarized contribution transfer confirmation from the remitting member.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, via the Supreme Court i-registration system or in-person counter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company to the District Court Registry. Attach the notarized Articles, capital contribution certificate, member identification passports, personal seal certificate of the Representative Director, digital certificate for electronic filing, and payment slips for registration tax and court fee. The court will review formal compliance with the Commercial Act and the Commercial Registration Rules. If the examiner issues a supplemental instruction, the applicant must file responsive documents promptly. Upon completion, the court enters the company in the corporate register and issues a certified corporate registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company
Capital contribution certificate or certificate of deposit
Power of attorney and agent identification if filed by agent
Registration tax and court fee payment slips
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplemental instruction, respond in writing within 14 days; if registration is refused, file an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act and correct the stated defect. In practice, a corrected refiling is accepted after exact compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-incorporation tax, bank, and statutory registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) district business registration office; local gu (municipal) office for local tax; and a licensed commercial bank for the permanent corporate account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after court registration, register the company for corporate income tax and value-added tax and obtain the Business Registration Certificate from the local National Tax Service district office. Open or convert the temporary bank account into the permanent corporate account using the corporate registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, and Representative Director identification. File a notice of incorporation with the NTS and report any employees to the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service. Notify the local gu office for local tax and business start-up status. Keep the corporate seal, registered office lease, and corporate register at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Representative Director identification and seal certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS delays issuance due to address or lease issues, submit a lease certificate and landlord identification; if bank anti-money-laundering review delays account opening, provide the board resolution, beneficial ownership declaration, source of funds evidence, and updated corporate documents.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS; Korean central tax authority). The statutory electronic portal is HomeTax (hometax.go.kr), which is the integrated system for business registration, VAT e-invoice submission, filing, and payment. Customs-side clearance is managed by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS trade facilitation system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company) formed in Korea: [1] complete corporate registration under the Korean Commercial Act with the competent registry court and obtain the corporate registration certificate. [2] Submit the statutory business registration application to the district tax office that has jurisdiction over the registered headquarters, via HomeTax or in writing, within the period required by Korean tax procedure law. The application must identify the corporation's legal name, registered address, actual principal office, representative director, main business activity (classified under ISIC 6201 / software and IT services), ownership structure, and banking details. [3] The NTS issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which is simultaneously the VAT registration number, the corporate income tax return reference number, and the mandatory identifier to be printed on tax invoices. [4] If the foreign shareholder is a non-resident entity that has not established a domestic Korean operation, the foreign entity must appoint and file a domestic tax representative with the NTS and obtain a non-resident business tax identifier through the HomeTax foreign business registration function. [5] All changes to registered particulars, including changes of address, representative, bank account, or business scope, must be amended through the same HomeTax application to keep the tax-ID record valid and to avoid administrative penalties. [6] Digital businesses selling to overseas customers should also request exporter identification registration with the Korea Customs Service and must retain the UNI-PASS exporter code, because the BRN remains the primary tax reference while the customs exporter code is required for export declarations in the UNI-PASS system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean corporate tax law does not provide a US-style check-the-box entity classification election. A Yuhan Hoesa is always a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax on its worldwide income. There is no pass-through entitlement. The only elective regimes that may be relevant are group-level consolidated tax filing for resident wholly-owned or substantially-held affiliates (subject to NTS approval) and the small/medium-sized enterprise or export-related tax reduction incentives that require a formal application; neither alters the default entity-level corporate tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW; no general registration threshold. Every person carrying on a business that supplies taxable goods or services in Korea must register with the NTS. A simplified taxable person status is available for a small business whose annual taxable turnover does not exceed KRW 80,000,000, but that status is not a registration exemption and the business still requires a VAT/tax identification number.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) system through the NTS HomeTax platform. Every VAT-registered business must issue a tax invoice containing the supplier BRN, purchaser BRN (for B2B supplies), supply date, supply value, VAT amount, and a unique e-invoice serial number, and must transmit the e-invoice to the HomeTax e-invoice system no later than the day after the invoice is issued. Electronic tax invoice transmission became mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses regardless of turnover from January 2022. There is no separate physical or cryptographic fiscal stamp applied before invoice issuance, but the NTS validates and stores every e-invoice centrally, and suspicious suppliers are flagged in the NTS anti-fraud data-analysis engine. For B2C card and cash sales, payment gateways and approved value-added-network operators transmit settlement data to the NTS Cash Receipt system on a real-time or near-real-time basis. The combination of e-tax invoices, cash receipts, and bank settlement data constitutes the anti-fraud clearance framework.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods qualify for the 0% VAT rate where the goods are exported to a foreign country and the export declaration is accepted by the Korea Customs Service; the goods must physically depart Korea and the export transaction must be supported by standard export documents. Cross-border services, including digital and cloud products such as the no-code website-builder subscriptions described in this dossier, qualify for 0% VAT where the service is supplied to a non-resident purchaser and the place of supply is treated as outside Korea under the Korean VAT Act. For B2B digital services, the place of supply is normally determined by the customer's place of business; for B2C digital services, the service is zero-rated when the foreign individual is resident outside Korea, payment is received in foreign currency, and the evidence demonstrates offshore access or consumption. Services physically performed in Korea, or services supplied to a Korean-resident customer, are taxable at the standard 10% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration accepted through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system (the definitive export evidence for physical goods; functionally the export bill of entry for Korean export law).
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (or an international courier export manifest / delivery confirmation in parcel exports) evidencing that the goods left the Republic of Korea.
Commercial invoice, packing list, and the zero-rated VAT e-tax invoice showing the 0% VAT rate.

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a licensed Korean foreign-exchange bank, or a functionally identical foreign-currency receipt confirmation, evidencing that the foreign currency export proceeds were received in Korea from the non-resident purchaser; in practice this is the Korean equivalent of a Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate required for 0% export-vat substantiation.

For digital service exports: the signed contract or online subscription agreement with the non-resident customer, the service-delivery log or IP/location data showing offshore use, the foreign-currency payment remittance record, and, where the customer is a foreign corporation, a foreign corporate registry extract or a self-certificate establishing its non-resident status.

Where export proceeds are paid after shipment, the foreign-exchange bank's export-settlement authorization or approved extension schedule must be retained to prove that the exporter received the funds within the statutory period.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service can retrospectively audit export zero-rating claims. If an export is found not to satisfy the zero-rating conditions, the NTS reclassifies the supply as a domestic taxable supply, assesses VAT at 10%, and adds statutory additional tax and overdue interest charges under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the VAT Act. The default assessment period is generally 5 years, extended to 10 years for deliberate concealment or tax evasion. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory Korean foreign-exchange settlement period (15 months from the export declaration, extendable by a licensed bank in limited cases) can lead to reversal of zero-rated treatment, recovery of unpaid VAT plus penalties, and administrative fines for violations of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, which may be up to 250% of the foreign currency not repatriated. In cases of intentionally false documentation, round-tripped payments, fake non-resident customers, or manipulated service-use data, the responsible entity and representative director may also face criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including imprisonment and fines calculated at multiples of the evaded tax. Accordingly, the compliance archive must preserve all export declarations, transport/receipt evidence, contracts, service-usage logs, payment remittance records, and the foreign-exchange bank confirmation for the full statutory retention period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized but tightly monitored foreign exchange system. Current account transactions, including digital service exports and ordinary business operating expenses, are broadly free and convertible at market rates through designated foreign exchange banks, with post-trade reporting rather than prior licensing. Capital account transactions are more restricted and require either advance declaration, registration, or approval before execution. A Yuhan Hoesa can receive foreign equity investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, but the capital funds must first arrive in a domestic foreign currency account at a designated bank and be reported before conversion into Korean won. Profit remittance is permitted once distributable reserves are certified by audited financial statements, but requires foreign exchange transaction reporting, payment of applicable withholding tax on dividends, a board resolution, corporate tax payment certificates, and proof that the investment was originally registered with the Korean authorities. Although there is no fixed statutory surrender ratio for export proceeds, the full amount of export earnings must be collected through a designated foreign exchange bank and repatriated into the Korean banking system within the statutory collection period or an approved extension. The practical hurdles are not convertibility itself but documentation: every material inbound and outbound flow must be traceable on the bank record, linked to an approved foreign exchange purpose code, and supported by contracts, invoices, tax certificates, and corporate resolutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected into a bank account at a designated foreign exchange bank within 18 months of the export date, unless an extension is approved by the foreign exchange authority. There is no mandatory conversion ratio, but the statutory export collection obligation requires 100% of the export invoice value to be received in Korea; the funds may be retained in a foreign currency account or converted to Korean won through the designated bank, and every receipt must be reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and Foreign Currency)
Capital Escrow Account and FDI Reporting Account
Basic Operational Currency Account with Digital Export Settlement
Capital Escrow Account and Dividend Remittance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low in Korea. A pure offshore fintech EMI is not legally equivalent to a designated foreign exchange bank and cannot serve as the principal treasury account for a Korean resident Yuhan Hoesa. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires corporate FX transactions, export collection, FDI capital receipt, and tax-related remittances to be routed through a bank registered in Korea. Offshore digital EMI platforms may be used only as ancillary SaaS billing rails, invoice presentment, or card acquisition networks, but all settlement must ultimately land in a domestic bank account. They also cannot perform capital verification, statutory export collection reporting, or dividend withholding documentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch physical presence is generally required for at least one statutory director or a registered signatory when opening a corporate account for a newly established Yuhan Hoesa. Remote consular proxy opening is only permitted in limited cases and requires a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, passport certification, original corporate registration certificate, Korean company seal or authorized signatory records, and a live video interview conducted by the bank compliance team. The bank will also inspect board resolutions confirming the opening of the account, the business plan, and the identity and source of funds of every ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign sole director and beneficial owner with no verifiable Korean banking history, triggering source-of-wealth uncertainty for the initial capital contribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies, apostilled entity formation documents, beneficial ownership declaration, 12 months personal and corporate bank statements from the shareholder, source-of-wealth narrative, CPA or tax accountant letter confirming the lawful origin of the shareholder funds, and a capital commitment resolution signed by the shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital no-code website builder generates revenue through Stripe and Paddle without traditional export invoices, bills of lading, or physical customs documentation, creating an intangible export evidence gap.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant of record agreements, customer subscription contracts, Stripe and Paddle settlement and payout reports, bank statements showing matching foreign currency receipts, subscriber and usage analytics dashboards, audited revenue reconciliations, and a certified tax accountant mapping each digital sale to Korean export reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder capitalization appears to be a related-party offshore loan rather than true equity, creating potential misclassification of capital account flow.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Promotion Act FDI registration certificate, bank-approved inward remittance report, share subscription agreement, share issuance board minutes, book-entry share register, remitter identification documents, source-of-funds evidence from the investing company, CRS tax self-certification, and an external auditor confirmation that the funds are equity and not disguised debt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient local substance for a digital exporter with no physical warehousing or goods flow, leading the bank to suspect shell activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate lease agreement for a Korean office, employment contracts and payroll records for at least two local staff, National Pension and health insurance submissions, board minutes confirming management decisions are made in Korea, utility bills, tax office business registration certificate, and a substance declaration listing local officers and their roles.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must be remitted by the non-resident investor through SWIFT MT103 to the Yuhan Hoesa foreign currency account at a designated South Korean bank using the Bank of Korea foreign exchange purpose code for foreign direct investment. The receiving bank executes the FDI report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, issues a foreign currency receipt confirmation, and after funds are verified the company may convert to Korean won. Capital verification is then performed by an independent statutory auditor who issues a capital verification report confirming the paid-in capital, share allocation, and compliance with the submitted FDI registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements run through the designated foreign exchange bank using SWIFT MT103 for direct payments and service royalties, commercial letters of credit via MT700 and MT707 for documentary trade, and documentary collections using DP/DA instructions through the bank's trade finance desk. For the no-code website builder, outbound payments for licensing, server costs, subcontractor fees, and refunds are cleared via MT103 with service or royalty purpose codes, supported by contracts, VAT invoices, and board-approved disbursement records. Any disbursement from the Capital Escrow Account is additionally checked against the approved business plan and the FDI-funded project scope.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: KRW/USD plain vanilla forward contracts approved by the designated foreign exchange bank, limited to 100% of verified underlying trade receivables or payables and a conventional tenor of up to 12 months
Non-deliverable forward hedges executed through authorized global bank counterparties when offshore settlement is required for USD/KRW exposure without physical Korean won delivery

Cross-currency interest rate swaps permitted for a Yuhan Hoesa holding foreign currency loans or foreign currency capex, provided the swap matches the notional, tenor, and debt service schedule of the underlying exposure

Zero-premium FX options and participating forwards for prudent hedging of digital subscription revenue, only where the underlying invoice flow is fully documented and no speculative position is created

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements must be executed by a designated foreign exchange bank. The standard clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for wire transfer disbursements, commercial letters of credit issued and confirmed through the SWIFT MT700/MT707 series, and documentary collections using DP/DA instructions through the bank trade finance desk. For a digital no-code website builder, outbound payments to overseas vendors, cloud providers, payment service providers, and licensing partners are normally cleared through SWIFT MT103 with the correct foreign exchange transaction purpose code, supported by service agreements, tax invoices, and board-approved disbursement memos.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: KRW/USD plain vanilla forward contracts allowed only when the company documents a genuine underlying trade receivable or payable within a matching maturity band

Non-deliverable forward contracts (NDFs) permitted solely for hedging USD/KRW exposure where physical Korean won settlement is not available through the counterparty and the hedge is benchmarked to the Seoul interbank rate
Cross-currency interest rate swaps allowed for hedges on underlying foreign currency loans or capital leases, with notional amount and maturity tied to the original debt exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year (within 3 months after fiscal year-end); may be extended to 30 April when filed with an authorized tax representative
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax (40% for fraudulent non-filing; 10% reduction if filed within 3 months after statutory deadline); additional daily interest at the statutory monthly rate (currently 0.022% per day) for outstanding tax; enforcement proceedings such as asset seizure and current business closure; persistent non-payment leads to registration cancellation and judicial dissolution strike-off from the commercial register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax (Local Inhabitants Surcharge) Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Government Authority (Si/Gun/Gu) through the Korea Local Tax Collection System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same due date as national corporate income tax return, generally by 31 March following the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% for non-payment within 10 days past due; monthly surcharge of 0.75% thereafter up to a maximum of 75%; compulsory collection, property seizure and cancellation of business registration for habitual delinquency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Enterprise Annual Status Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) via Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or a registered Foreign Exchange Bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the fiscal year (by 30 January for December fiscal year-end enterprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 1 million (approximately USD 750) under Article 27 FIPA; repeat non-compliance may lead to modification or revocation of foreign investment registration, forfeiture of tax benefits, and restricted dividend/remittance privileges

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Filing (DART submission) - applicable only when the KRW 10 billion year-end total asset threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) through the Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System (DART)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent auditor's report must be issued before the annual general meeting of members (AGM) and the audited financial statements must be submitted to FSC/DART within 10 days after the date of the AGM (AGM must be held by 31 March or the statutory permitted extension)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties under the Act on External Audit of Corporations: fine up to KRW 50 million (approximately USD 37,000) for violating audit appointment/filing obligations; non-submission of audit report leads to administrative fines, enforcement of FSC corrective orders and, for listed effects, forced removal from DART; the company loses ability to rely on audited financials for shareholder approvals

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Corporations (Act No. 15896) and its Enforcement Decree, an independent audit by a certified public accountant is legally required when, at the end of the reporting fiscal year: (a) total assets amount to KRW 10 billion or more (approximately USD 7.5 million); or (b) the company is a 'public interest company' under Article 2, including companies with listed securities, companies with total assets of KRW 200 billion or more, and designated financial institutions; or (c) the company has previously issued public bonds or holds a registration under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act. There is no separate turnover or headcount trigger for a standard private LLC; however, a company with 500 or more full-time employees may be considered a large-scale private firm and will require external audit if group consolidated total assets exceed the threshold. In addition, lenders or foreign parents may contractually require an audit under K-IFRS even if the statutory threshold is not met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for public interest companies and consolidated groups; non-public corporations, including a private Yuhan Hoesa, may apply K-IFRS or the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP, specifically the 'General Corporate Accounting Standards' issued by the Korean Financial Supervisory Service) for statutory financial statements. For an entity below the audit threshold, financial statements must still be prepared on a basis consistent with the Korean Commercial Act and the Corporate Tax Act, using either K-IFRS or K-GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) requires annual confirmation of beneficial ownership through the Foreign Investment Enterprise Annual Status Report, due within 30 days after the end of each fiscal year (31 January for a December year-end). Any shareholding transfer had to be reported initially within 30 days of the transaction (via the foreign exchange bank or KOTRA) and any resulting change to the foreign investment ratio must also be filed as an amended foreign investment registration. Additionally, under the revised Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information and the Real Name Financial Transactions Act, the Company must verify and maintain the beneficial ownership profile of its members at least once a year in connection with financial services relationships; notifications of any UBO change must be delivered to the financial institution within 30 days. All share transfers not registered by the company are ineffective against third parties under the Korean Commercial Act.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (including foreign investment nationality and capital contribution records)
Register of Directors (where a board director structure has been elected)
Minute Book of Members' General Meetings and Board Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 18,000 per audit engagement (where threshold is triggered or group reporting requires it)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion (progressive corporate income tax schedule under the Korean Corporate Tax Act)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small and medium enterprise preferential tax rates, tax holiday and 50% income tax reduction for qualified foreign-invested high-technology businesses under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, R&D tax credits (including growth-stage and national strategic technology investment credits), special reserve for investment, and digital content and software development tax incentives; after these incentives the effective rate for a qualifying Yuhan Hoesa can be materially below the headline rate, but a minimum tax is imposed when normal tax credits exceed a statutory ceiling.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return and Taxable Base & Tax Computation Schedule (Form 1 / Annex 1) filed electronically through the National Tax Service Hometax portal; the return package includes the financial statements schedule, tax adjustment schedule, foreign tax credit schedule, and non-resident withholding declaration schedule.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within three months after the fiscal year end; for a December year end the deadline is March 31, with a permitted extension of up to one month for foreign-owned corporations and additional time for groups whose financial statements are audited overseas. Failure to file with extension triggers the penalties listed below.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross turnover from sales of no-code website templates, visual web template subscriptions, low-code application builder access fees, consulting, and related software licensing revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Yuhan Hoesa must declare worldwide income because it is a Korean domestic corporation. Foreign-currency revenue is converted into Korean won at the Bank of Korea base rate on the transaction date or the last business day of the fiscal year. Do not net out Stripe/Paddle processing fees, chargeback costs, marketplace commissions, or VAT-like foreign taxes; those are separately deductible expenses. If a foreign reseller receives the initial payment, the substance of the sale contract determines whether the revenue is attributable to a Korean permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to revenue: cloud hosting, API usage fees, domain registration, template author payments, contracted front-end developers, software license procurement, and server infrastructure costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility of costs paid to a non-resident related party requires written contracts, actual service evidence, and an arm's length price under the Act for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. If the foreign supplier or template author is a treaty-resident person, royalty payments must be reviewed for withholding tax; failure to withhold on a taxable cross-border payment will be treated as a non-deductible expense and assessed as unresolved withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 3a - Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing expenses, payment gateway fees, salaries, outsourced support, legal and accounting services, IT security costs, office rent, and general overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany service fees, marketing fees, and management fees from a foreign parent or affiliate must satisfy the benefit test and be reasonably allocated to the Korean entity's revenue-generating activities. Pure shareholder costs are non-deductible. Payments to non-resident platform providers such as app-store operators, advertising networks, or data processors may be chargeable to Korean withholding tax if they are not strictly business profits; the return must attach a complete reconciliation of foreign service fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Line 4a - Tax Adjustments: Additions and Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book-to-tax reconciliation entries: non-deductible penalties, entertainment allowance in excess of statutory limits, charitable contribution carryovers, bad debt additions and reversals, R&D special expensing, non-taxable income, and foreign exchange gains or losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border controlled transactions must be restated to the arm's length result in this section. An excessive intercompany royalty paid to the foreign parent is added back to taxable income as a non-deductible expense. If the Korean entity previously claimed a treaty-protected royalty or service payment, the tax adjustment schedule must preserve the evidence that the recipient actually performed the services and is the beneficial owner; a dormant foreign shell disqualifies the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 5a - Taxable Income Before Loss Carryforward / Tax Base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss carryforward, then after applying the deductible net operating loss carryforward from prior years, yielding the final corporate income tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the loss carryforward strictly within the five-year statutory window used at this compliance stage. Losses generated during a period when the entity was a paper shell, or losses attributable to foreign branches that were ineligible for domestic tax relief, must be excluded. The tax base is never negative and cannot be reduced by the foreign parent's losses, by shareholder capital contributions, or by distributions treated as loans.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 6a - Corporate Income Tax Computation and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the tentative corporate income tax using the progressive rate schedule, then subtract statutory tax credits including R&D credits, employment credits, investment tax credits, and foreign tax credits; finally apply any minimum tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: At this box the Korean corporate income tax is a separate entity-level tax. Foreign tax credits are allowed only for foreign income taxes paid on profits that are included in the Korean tax base, and are limited to the lesser of the foreign tax paid or the Korean corporate tax attributable to that foreign income. Dividends payable to a non-resident shareholder are not deductible and cannot be netted against the computed corporate tax. The entity must not reduce its Korean tax by any anticipated tax treaty withholding reduction on the distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Attached Schedule - Local Income Tax Surcharge and Non-Resident Dividend Withholding Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local corporate income tax surcharge (10% of the amount computed in Box 6) and the attached schedule reporting dividends or other distributions paid or payable to non-resident shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local surcharge increases the effective direct corporate tax burden. For the non-resident shareholder, dividend withholding tax is 22% absent a treaty: 20% national income tax plus 2% local inflation subcharge. To claim a lower DTA rate, attach the shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, the beneficial ownership declaration, a shareholding and holding-period analysis, and the applicable Korea treaty provisions; the reduced treaty rate may be used only after the Korean payer holds all supporting documents at the payment date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and non-filing penalties are imposed under the Framework Act on National Taxes Articles 47-3 to 47-5: a return filed after deadline without reasonable cause attracts the unreported return negligence tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax, while filing an understated or false return attracts an underreporting negligence tax of 10% (or 40% for fraudulent false returns). In addition, the National Tax Service imposes a daily overdue charge of about 0.022% per day from the statutory due date until actual payment, plus the local income tax surcharge penalty. Criminal sanctions apply when the underreporting is intentional and substantial: the taxpayer or representative director may be prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment and fines up to several times the evaded tax, and the National Tax Service may issue a public blacklisting notice and a travel restriction order while the criminal investigation is pending.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national income tax under Income Tax Act Article 98(2), plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the national tax = 2 percentage points), before any bilateral tax treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced rate under a DTA, the Korean payer must obtain from the foreign shareholder, before the WHT payment date: (1) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the shareholder's residence country covering the relevant year; (2) a completed declaration of beneficial ownership showing the shareholder is the true economic owner of the dividend, interest, or royalty and not a conduit; (3) a certificate of business substance and, if the shareholder is the parent of the Yuhan Hoesa, the shareholding structure; and (4) a specific treaty relief application submitted through the Hometax portal. If the documentation is incomplete or the non-resident is a zero-tax shell with no personnel, office, decision-making authority, or economic risk, the tax authority will disregard the treaty claim, retroactively collect the full 22% WHT, add negligence penalties and late-payment surcharges, and refer the directors to the criminal tax authorities.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates for non-resident recipients are 20% national income tax plus 2% local surcharge, totaling 22% for both interest and royalty income. Under a DTA, interest rates are frequently reduced to 10% or 15% depending on the lender's status; royalty rates for software and website template copyright are often reduced to 10% or 15% but only where Korea's treaty royalty definition includes software payments and the beneficial owner carries on economic activities in the treaty country. Payments that are transactions between the Korean LLC and its non-resident parent should be re-checked for transfer pricing substance before treaty withholding relief is granted.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The Korean entity is required to prepare and submit a transfer pricing Local File and Master File when the annual gross turnover exceeds KRW 100 billion and the combined volume of international related-party transactions exceeds KRW 50 billion; a simplified TP disclosure schedule is required where cross-border related-party controlled transactions exceed the lower KRW 5 billion threshold. Even below the mandatory documentation threshold, the Yuhan Hoesa must maintain contemporaneous evidence of the arm's length price for any cross-border intercompany royalties, service fees, cloud infrastructure charges, or software distribution arrangements.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, but it applies the anti-abuse doctrine of substance over form under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Act for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. The Yuhan Hoesa must actually perform Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Korea: a real office, real employees, Thai board and management decisions, ownership and control over the intellectual property of the no-code website templates, active customer contracts, and day-to-day product development. A Korean registered company that does not have CIGA will be treated as a shell, its Korean tax residence may be challenged, and treaty benefits, permanent establishment protection, and withholding reductions can be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by Suppressing Gross Revenue and Using Offshore Payment Routes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting revenue from foreign no-code website template subscriptions and low-code platform coffee while the contracts, servers, accounts, and management decisions are all located in Korea; diverting sales proceeds to a foreign bank account or shell company; recording actual customer subscriptions as non-interest-bearing shareholder loans or fake shareholder capital.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, a fraudulent return or fraudulent evasion of Korean corporate income tax is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years and a fine of up to five times the evaded tax. The National Tax Service additionally applies the 20% unregistered or 40% fraudulent understatement negligence tax under Articles 47-3 to 47-5 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, together with a daily overdue charge until full payment, and may blacklist the company as a habitual high-risk tax debtor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director and any de facto director who signed the false return or instructed the use of the offshore route is personally liable under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act for the unpaid corporate tax plus penalties to the extent of the personal assets of the director. Criminal prosecution may lead to imprisonment, a travel ban, seizure of personal real estate, bank accounts, and shares, and disqualification from serving as a director. The civil asset restitution obligation extends to corporate property that was dissipated through the foreign shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Transfer Pricing and Defective Intercompany Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Yuhan Hoesa pays a foreign parent or affiliate a high intercompany royalty or service fee for the use of the low-code platform software brand or vendor code, while the affiliate does not perform actual services, has no employees, and has no economic substance; no Local File or Master File is prepared; no benchmarking study supports the selected profit margin; and the Korean entity deliberately leaves into loss from year one under the inflated deductible payments to a related overseas entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may adjust the intercompany consideration to arm's length under Articles 4 and 5 of the Act for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, disallow the excessive intercompany fees, impose the unfaithful-report negligence tax on the resulting underpaid corporate tax, assess a transfer pricing penalty for failure to supply contemporaneous documentation when requested, and add late-payment surcharges. The NTS may also characterize the transaction as tax fraud if the documents are fabricated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the sham intercompany agreement are jointly and severally liable for the additional tax under the National Tax Collection Act Article 39. In an intentional transfer pricing arrangement, the director can be criminally prosecuted for tax evasion by way of artificial profit shifting, with a travel ban, an asset attachment order, and imprisonment risk; the corporate veil is pierced to recover hidden profits and unpaid penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Shopping, Shell Beneficial Owner, and Improper Dividend/Royalty WHT Reduction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Attracting the payment of Korean dividends, royalties, or interest to a zero-tax or low-tax company in Singapore, Hong Kong, the United States, or another treaty country that does not have any real business, employees, offices, contractual risk, or significant decision-making authority over the software; the shell is interposed exclusively to obtain the benefits of a DTA and to avoid the Korean 22% statutory withholding tax; the non-resident itself is ultimately controlled by the Korean director or Korean shareholders, or the dividend/royalty is immediately redistributed to a third country without economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service will deny the treaty benefits under the beneficial ownership rule and under Korea's anti-treaty-abuse rules in Article 98-6 of the Income Tax Act and Article 9 of the Act for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, assess the unpaid 22% withholding tax plus the local surcharge, impose the 20%/40% unregistered return penalty, and demand late-payment surcharges. The payer company is jointly liable for failing to withhold the statutory amount even though the DTA claim was presented.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who executed a false treaty withholding declaration without a Tax Residency Certificate or without verifying beneficial ownership are personally responsible for the uncollected withholding tax under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act. Criminal prosecution is available where the treaty evasion is intentional and large; the director can face imprisonment, a travel ban, personal asset seizure, and permanent blacklisting, while the foreign shell remains vulnerable to disqualification and threatened from public filing.
